quarantine.oracle: P(parse(x)) == P(parse(T(x))) where P extracts all meta-information lines as a set (ignoring order), and the data records are identical

evidence.quote: Meta-information lines can appear in any order, with the exception that the ##fileformat line must be the first line of the file.

quarantine.mr_name: Structured header key-value pair order invariance
quarantine.oracle: P(parse(x)) == P(parse(T(x))) where P extracts the structured header definitions as sets of key=value pairs, ignoring their order within each structured line

evidence.quote: The order of key=value pairs within a structured meta-information line is not significant.

quarantine.oracle: P(parse(x)) == P(parse(T(x))) where P extracts INFO field values as a key-value map, ignoring the order of semicolon-separated entries

evidence.quote: INFO fields are encoded as semicolon-separated key=value pairs; the order of these pairs is not significant.

quarantine.oracle: P(parse(x)) == P(parse(T(x))) where P extracts sample genotype data as a set of (sample_id, genotype) pairs, ignoring column ordering

evidence.quote: The order of sample columns in the VCF file is not semantically meaningful; each sample is identified by its column header.

quarantine.oracle: P(parse(x)) == P(parse(T(x))) where P extracts the canonical JSON representation; BCF codec re-indexes dictionary entries so order is irrelevant

evidence.quote: The order of dictionary entries in the BCF header is implementation-defined; parsers must use the dictionary index to resolve types, not the declaration order.
